title: Comparing memory capacity across stimuli requires maximally dissimilar foils: Using deep convolutional neural networks to understand visual working memory capacity for real-world objects
authors: Timothy F. Brady, Viola S. Störmer
caption_short: Method of Experiment 2: participants saw six real-world objects for 2000 ms, held them over a 700 ms delay, and then made a two-alternative forced choice at a cued location between the studied object and a foil.

notes: Cropped from page 8 (journal page 602) of the published typeset PDF at 440 dpi; caption text excluded. Fig. 4 shows the full trial: 6-object memory array (2000 ms, spatial placeholders visible throughout) -> 700 ms delay -> 2-AFC test at one cued location with the studied object and one foil. The foil-similarity manipulation is described in the caption rather than drawn as separate panels: foils were maximally distinct cross-category, minimally distinct cross-category, or randomly chosen from a different category (60 trials each, 180 total, N = 50 MTurk participants). The example pairs for the similarity conditions are shown separately in Fig. 2, and the CNN foil-selection method in Fig. 1. Fig. 6 (page 10) is the analogous method figure for Experiment 3, which contrasts objects with colors.
